title: HLabs: typescript cardano-node / consensus (node prototype) - NodeJS target runtime relay node

ms.promise:
・managing connections from other nodes in the network
・parse headers in the receiving chain-sync messages
・parse bodies in the receiving block-fetch messages
・test for correctness, especially for header hashes
ms.criteria:
a new repository is created on HarmonicLabs' github for ouroboros-consensus-ts
the code in the repo includes the outputs specified above, in particular:
・is aware and can handle connections with peers
・can parse incoming messages
・does not alterate the data to preserve hases

ms.promise:
the node can use everything implemented in the previous milestones to:
・verify incoming blocks 
・select the honest chain based on known blocks and ledger state.
・of course appropriate unit tests are also an output of the milestone.

the node can follow many chains, handle soft forks, and stay on the honest chain.
ms.criteria: the node can follow many chains, handle soft forks, and stay on the honest chain.
ms.report:
here is the video showcasing the current node performing chain selection and the implementation of the volatile db: https://youtu.be/B76yiK_XlrY
We are currently testing the node by just running it as it was shown in the video
We cannot produce forks on our own (that depends on the blockchain) here is attached an image of one time we found a fork and handled it successfully: https://postimg.cc/vg7KfxYK

ms.promise:
The node now stores historical data and accepts and validates transactions.
This is the minimum viable node for dApps.
ms.criteria:
To make sure the outputs above are valid
The node should:
・always follow the longest chain
・keep track of possible soft forks that in the future might become the longest chain
・reject any forks longer than the security parameter k (about 36 hours)
ms.report:
Just like the previous milestone, we are currently testing the node by just running it as shown in the video.

here is the video showcasing the current node implementation: https://youtu.be/u9vjIYEB7ho

In the video we showcase how we can retrieve historical blocks (which proves the blocks are stored in the immutable db)
the video also shows how we can submit and validate transaction through the node and propagate to other nodes.

These are the basic functionalities that are needed for a minimum viable node.

Of course there is still work to do that is not covered in this project, but with this milestone we get gerolamo significantly closer to production.

(apologies for the "acceptance criteria" section, it would seem the one that would be of the previous milestone are shown here)
